articles.title: NFL suspends official Jeff Seeman for two games for swearing at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride
articles.summary: The NFL suspended two officials for separate incidents on Sunday, including Jeff Seeman after he was caught swearing at Arizona's Trey McBride; watch the second NFL London game of the season between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles at 2.30pm Sunday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Jeff Seeman was caught on camera cursing at McBride during the Cardinals' loss to the New York Giants on Sunday.

"Obviously, you hate to see it, for obvious reasons," Arizona coach Mike LaFleur said. "I do want to give the man a little bit of grace, too. I know Jeff. He's a good man. It's unfortunate it happened. It can't happen, obviously, and I'll leave it at that."

The incident drew the ire of union leader JC Tretter, a retired offensive lineman who played eight seasons.

"This kind of behaviour from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter, the NFL Players Association's executive director, said on social media along with a video clip of the incident.

"Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

The interaction took place with just under five minutes left after officials did not call a pass interference or illegal contact penalty on New York's Dru Phillips, who made contact with McBride before the ball arrived from Jacoby Brissett on a third-and-two play.

Arizona punted and the Giants went on to win 36-24 after Deonte Banks intercepted Brissett's pass and ran it back for a pick-6 as time expired.

Referee Adrian Hill was also suspended one game for unprofessional conduct in the Miami-Minnesota game. Hill yelled at Eric Wilson and pointed for him to get away after the Vikings linebacker tried to help him to his feet after a collision knocked him over.

"I just think it's one of those situations in kind of a high-energy moment there," Minnesota coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.

"I think stuff like that can happen sometimes, but I don't have any major concerns, and I think Adrian's a really good official and does a really good job. I think that was just kind of fast moment that happened, and we can put it behind us, hopefully."

The league's vice president of officiating, Ramon George, issued the suspensions. The NFL Referees Association did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

This isn't the first time an official has been punished for interactions with a player on the field.

Umpire Roy Ellison was punished twice for his behavior. In 2018, he was fined $9,300 and placed on administrative leave for one game after he was accused of calling Buffalo defensive end Jerry Hughes a derogatory term.

Ellison was also suspended for one game in 2013 for making "a profane and derogatory statement" to Washington left tackle Trent Williams

articles.title: NFL Week 4 injury roundup: Lamar Jackson, Ja’Marr Chase and Saquon Barkley among stars raising Week 5 concerns
articles.summary: The NFL’s Week 4 injury list could have a real effect on several teams heading into Week 5.
articles.body: The NFL’s Week 4 injury list could have a real effect on several teams heading into Week 5. Ja’Marr Chase is in concussion protocol, Saquon Barkley is dealing with a hamstring injury and Lamar Jackson has an ankle issue that has already left him in a walking boot. Those are not the only concerns. Kansas City lost Tyquan Thornton to a serious ankle injury, Arizona’s Paris Johnson Jr. is out for the season, and Green Bay’s Edgerrin Cooper also suffered a season-ending Achilles tear. The next few days will be important as teams wait for updates on key players.What is the latest on Ja’Marr Chase and Saquon Barkley?Chase’s injury could be particularly costly for Cincinnati. The Bengals fell to 2-2 after losing to Jacksonville, then watched their biggest offensive weapon leave with a concussion. Chase did not return after being evaluated and is now in the NFL’s concussion protocol.His availability for Week 5 will depend on how he progresses through the league’s steps. Cincinnati also has another concern at receiver. Tee Higgins suffered an adductor injury and is considered day-to-day, leaving the Bengals potentially short on their top two pass catchers.Philadelphia has its own offensive issue with Barkley. The Eagles running back suffered a hamstring injury against the Los Angeles Rams and is now considered week-to-week. His status for Week 5 remains unclear.Barkley’s workload has already drawn attention this season, so the timing of the injury adds another layer to Philadelphia’s situation. The Eagles will need to be careful with a player whose explosiveness is central to their offense.Is Lamar Jackson expected to play in Week 5?Baltimore has received some relief on that front, at least for now. Jackson suffered an ankle injury during the Ravens’ Week 4 win over Tennessee and was seen wearing a walking boot afterward.That image naturally raised concern about the quarterback’s availability. However, the injury is currently considered day-to-day. That gives Baltimore some hope that Jackson will avoid an extended absence, although his practice participation will likely be closely watched throughout the week.The Ravens have started the season strongly, making Jackson’s health especially important. Even a short absence would force Baltimore to adjust an offense that is built heavily around his ability to create plays with both his arm and legs.Which other NFL stars suffered significant injuries?Kansas City faces a more serious situation with Thornton. He scored twice against Las Vegas before suffering a dislocated left ankle late in the game. His ankle was reset, but he is out indefinitely while further testing is completed. Rashee Rice also left that game with a hamstring injury.Arizona has lost Johnson for the rest of the season because of a biceps injury. Green Bay will also be without Cooper after he tore his Achilles tendon.Denver received better news on Patrick Surtain, whose ankle injury is considered short-term. articles.title: Will Shipley and the Best Week 5 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: The first month of the 2026 NFL season is complete and the coinciding fantasy football campaign has been nothing short of wild.
articles.body:
The first month of the 2026 NFL season is complete and the coinciding fantasy football campaign has been nothing short of wild.

With a slew of major injuries striking some of the league's biggest stars, managers have been scrambling to line up replacements and keep their team afloat.

Week 5 marks the start of byes, throwing an additional wrench into the mix for fantasy managers to contend with. While only the Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs will be out this week, it's now imperative to have good backups in place to withstand the wave of upcoming byes and inevitable injuries.

Whether you've been steadily turning over the bottom of your roster with free agents or have yet to tinker with the squad you've drafted, Week 5 represents an ideal time to dive into the waiver wire and find some solid talent.

While there aren't any obvious league-winners sticking out right now, there are plenty of serviceable options who can fill holes in your starting lineup and provide depth for the long road ahead.

With that in mind, let's look at the top waiver-wire pickups for Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (23 Percent Rostered)

Cousins is thriving at the reins of the Raiders, keeping the club in contention while staving off what initially seemed to be an inevitable takeover of the starting role by prized rookie Fernando Mendoza.

Cousins is firmly in the QB1 fantasy discussion after he followed up three consecutive top-12 performances with a gem against the Kansas City Chiefs. While the Raiders took their first loss of the campaign, their signal-caller put up a season-best 23.6 points and earned a top-five finish in a 30-27 defeat to the Kansas City Chiefs.

First-year head coach Klint Kubiak obviously trusts Cousins to carry the offense. After averaging a shade over 30 passing attempts per game during September, the 15th-year veteran aired it out a whopping 52 times on Sunday. He connected on 31 of those throws, generating 365 yards and two touchdowns.

While Cousins has not been perfect—his four interceptions are tied for the third-most in football—he should be rostered in far more leagues than he currently is.

If you need a replacement QB to get you through more than just Week 5, you need not look any further than Cousins.

Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (10 Percent Rostered)

Rodgers began his 2026 season as tepid as ever, amassing just 17.5 fantasy points over the first two weeks. Despite the slow start, the longtime veteran has quietly emerged as one of the better fantasy quarterbacks of the past two weeks.

The Steelers' offense has come to life behind the play of its 42-year-old leader, with Rodgers lighting up both the Cincinnati Bengals and Cleveland Browns for nearly 300 passing yards and three touchdowns apiece.

He finished as the QB8 in Week 3 before going on to cement his first top-five finish since landing in Pittsburgh with a 24-point effort during his team's Thursday Night Football showcase.

Rodgers has an opportunity to continue his string of QB1-tier performance in Week 5 when he squares off against the Indianapolis Colts.

Indy's defense has allowed an average of 20.5 points per game to opposing passers in 2026, making Rodgers a strong plug-and-play choice for those streaming the quarterback position.

C.J. Stroud, Houston Texans (58 Percent Rostered)

Stroud was abandoned in many leagues after he failed to work as a serviceable fantasy quarterback during the month of September. The calendar flipping—plus the return of his top receiver—seems to have rejuvenated the Houston passer.

With Nico Collins back in action for the first time since the opener, Stroud put up a season-best 23.1 points.

By completing 21-of-31 throws for 347 yards and two touchdowns, Stroud not only kept his Texans competitive during a shootout against the Dallas Cowboys, but he also showed that he may still have some fantasy value outside of 2QB and superflex formats.

It remains to be seen if he can keep it rolling against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5, but with injuries at the position mounting and bye weeks beginning, he could be worth rolling the dice on.

Will Shipley, Philadelphia Eagles (2 Percent Rostered)

The Eagles' backfield was decimated by injury during Sunday's 24-20 defeat to the Los Angeles Rams.

Star running back Saquon Barkley was knocked out of the contest early with a hamstring problem, and backup Tank Bigsby went down late with a core muscle issue.

Per ESPN's Tim McManus , Barkley avoided an IR stint and hasn't been officially declared out for Week 5, but he is considered week-to-week as he works his way back from the hamstring injury. Bigsby will be out longer due to a surgical procedure that will take approximately six weeks to recover from.

Will Shipley is now the last man standing in Philadelphia's platoon and is set to become its feature back, at least for a stretch. Considering he's likely to be the only established rusher ready to go for the team's upcoming clash in London with the Jacksonville Jaguars, he has potential RB2 value for this contest and possibly beyond.

While the Eagles will need to make some moves to reinforce the backfield before the game (practice squad members Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and Jaydon Blue are the top candidates), Shipley projects to see the lion's share of volume and can be started with confidence.

Emanuel Wilson, Seattle Seahawks (49 Percent Rostered)

Wilson may have disappointed those who added him as a trendy waiver-wire pickup following a 21-carry effort in Week 2, but he delivered on Sunday.

The journeyman running back put up 27 fantasy points to help his side earn a 30-23 victory over the reeling Los Angeles Chargers.

First-round rookie Jadarian Price missed the game with a chest injury and will have to sit three more contests at a minimum after landing on the IR.

Making his first start as a Seahawk, Wilson picked up 81 rushing yards and a touchdown on 21 totes and got involved as a pass-catcher for the first time this season, reeling in three of four targets for 39 yards and another score.

Wilson profiles as a low-end RB2 for Seattle's upcoming bout against the San Francisco 49ers. He should retain that status until Price and/or Zach Charbonnet (who just practiced for the first time since suffering a major knee injury in last season's playoffs) return to action. He may not have the best long-term outlook, but any manager lacking quality backs at this point in the campaign should make a run at Wilson.

Brian Robinson Jr., Atlanta Falcons (31 Percent Rostered)

Bijan Robinson may have been the star of Atlanta's big Monday Night Football win over the New Orleans Saints, but his backup got heavily involved in the action as well.

Brian Robinson Jr. finished the 45-24 blowout with a sizzling 25.7 fantasy points after exploding for 62 yards and three touchdowns on 14 totes.

Despite the outburst, Robinson doesn't have too much standalone value. He posted his first double-digit scoring day of the season in Week 3, after two quiet two games to open the 2026 campaign.

While managers shouldn't roster Robinson expecting similar results to Monday night with any frequency, he's established himself as the league's top handcuff.

Bijan Robinson is the engine that is driving Atlanta's resurgent offense, a role that Brian Robinson would step directly into if the starter misses any time. He's a must-add right now for that value alone.

Chris Rodriguez, Jacksonville Jaguars (37 Percent Rostered)

Bhayshul Tuten is Jacksonville's top back, but Rodriguez has been making some noise as the backup. Rodriguez had his second consecutive top-30 fantasy outing on Sunday, finishing a 22-17 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals with 9.5 points.

Although Rodriguez only logged six carries in the contest, he generated a solid 35 yards and a touchdown with them. The performance followed on the heels of a 9.7-point showing in Week 3 in which the rusher tallied 37 yards and a score on eight carries.

Rodriguez may only have flex appeal in deeper leagues due to his touchdown-dependency, but he's a Tuten injury away from stepping into a far bigger role. Stash him if you can afford the bench spot.

Keon Coleman, Buffalo Bills (5 Percent Rostered)

Coleman's already-tanking fantasy value truly plummeted when the Bills added D.J. Moore this offseason, but it's looking like he's back on the radar now that the team's top wideout could miss some time.

Moore exited Sunday's contest after reaggravating a nagging shoulder injury in a 29-26 defeat to the New England Patriots, opening the door for Coleman to take on a larger role.

Coleman has already begun to capitalize on the uptick in usage, finishing the contest with season-best marks of six catches, 116 receiving yards and one touchdown. His 23.6 fantasy points represented his most since the 2025 season opener.

While Coleman needs to hit the bench if Moore is active—the third-year receiver didn't garner more than four targets in any of the first three games—he's worth an add right now and can be inserted into starting lineups if his counterpart is sitting.

Romeo Doubs, New England Patriots (57 Percent Rostered)

Although Doubs is owned in a bit more than half of all fantasy leagues, it's still worth checking your free-agent pile to see if he's available.

Managers may have given up on the Patriots wideout after he mustered a combined 20.5 fantasy points over the first three weeks, a decision they'll regret following an explosive Week 4 performance that makes him a must-add in any league he's available in.

Doubs finally asserted himself as the No. 1 WR the Patriots have sorely needed since losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain in the opener. The veteran torched the Buffalo Bills defense for 58 yards and a pair of touchdowns, making the most of his team-high nine targets during the team's 29-26 victory.

While the NFL Network's Mike Garofolo reported that New England is hopeful Brown will return to the lineup in Week 6, Doubs is a slam-dunk fantasy starter for the team's upcoming matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

He also has plenty of upside to remain fantasy relevant beyond that, especially if star QB Drake Maye can return to the MVP-level of play he displayed for much of the 2025 campaign.

Tre' Harris, Los Angeles Chargers (9 Percent Rostered)

The Bolts need to shake things up after a brutal 0-4 start to the 2026 NFL season and Harris could move up the depth chart as part of these adjustments.

Harris has been L.A.'s most productive wideout over the first month of the campaign, tallying 13 catches and 209 receiving yards on 21 targets.

Star wideout Ladd McConkey (12/183/1 on 17 targets) has been dealing with several injuries, while No. 2 pass-catcher Quentin Johnston (7/108/0 on 18 targets) remains as inconsistent as ever.

Harris has been picking up the slack and earning the trust of the coaching staff, resulting in him logging a season-high of 66 offensive snaps in Week 4. If he continues to see that type of playing time and the Chargers can figure things out offensively, it wouldn't be a surprise to see Harris break out as a weekly fantasy starter.

Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders (6 Percent Rostered)

With star wideout Terry McLaurin a late scratch for Week 4 after picking up a hamstring injury in practice, Williams moved up a notch in Washington's pecking order.

While the bump in targets didn't quite translate to noteworthy production (he only mustered three catches for 21 yards on eight looks after an 87-yard TD was called back due to a procedural penalty), Williams' usage rate is extremely promising for fantasy purposes.

Washington's quarterback situation remains messy after backup Marcus Mariota went down with a knee injury in Week 4 and joined starter Jayden Daniels on the sidelines, but the team's abysmal defense will likely force whoever is lining up under center to air it out often.

The Commanders have allowed 30-plus points in each of the last three contests, a stretch during which their quarterbacks have averaged nearly 35 throws per game.

Williams has WR3 potential if McLaurin remains out, but the rookie third-rounder's unique slot and gadget role within the offense even gives him some upside in a full-strength Washington receiving corps.

Roman Wilson, Pittsburgh Steelers (3 Percent Rostered)

No one expected that Wilson would become the top wideout on a Steelers squad that features both DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr.

Although it initially seemed he might be a flash in the pan, the third-year wideout has remained the offense's most consistent pass-catcher over the first month of the 2026 season.

With six targets in each of Pittsburgh's first four games and production improving each week, Wilson has established himself as a viable flex option for fantasy. He's coming off a career-best outing against the Cleveland Browns, reeling in three catches for 74 yards and a second consecutive touchdown. He's now logged top-25 finishes in each of the past two weeks.

While the Steelers must get Metcalf and Pittman more involved if they have any serious aspirations to contend, Wilson is earning quarterback Aaron Rodgers' trust.

Expect him to parlay that chemistry into a higher offensive snap share and a potential nice fantasy day when the Steelers square off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5.

T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings (30 Percent Rostered)

Injuries have severely limited Hockenson's output in recent seasons, but the Minnesota tight end turned back the clock on Sunday. He secured all 13 targets that came his way, picking up 119 yards to rate as the top-scoring fantasy player at his position in Week 4.

While Minnesota remained undefeated thanks to Hockenson's 24.9-point effort, much of his production occurred due to the absence of Justin Jefferson.

Managers will want to monitor the wideout's status leading up to the team's Week 5 battle against the New Orleans Saints, as Hockenson will be a set-and-forget TE1 if Jefferson were to miss more time.

Managers seeking a long-term option could also consider Hockenson. He's building a fast rapport with quarterback Kyler Murray and has benefitted from a higher offensive snap share since fellow TE Josh Oliver suffered a torn biceps that landed him on the IR.

Mike Gesicki, Cincinnati Bengals (7 Percent Rostered)

Gesicki has been a scoring machine to open the 2026 NFL season. He's pulled down a touchdown in three of the first four games, making him the rare consistent performer who is still surprisingly widely available at a position that has been bereft of serviceable waiver options.

Gesicki posted a 3/40/1 line on five targets during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. His 13 fantasy points marked his third double-digit outing and third TE12 or better finish of the campaign.

While Gesicki isn't seeing enough targets to continue putting up TE1-tier numbers if he doesn't find pay dirt, the 6'6", 245-pounder has become one of quarterback Joe Burrow's favorite targets in the red area and is a threat to haul in a score in every week.

Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars (27 Percent Rostered)

Strange hasn't lived up to his status as a popular sleeper choice leading up to the 2026 campaign, but he could be on the cusp of turning things around. He's coming off his best performance of the season and could potentially use that as a springboard to the type of weekly numbers managers were hoping for.

Strange feasted against the Cincinnati Bengals defense, hauling in seven of his eight targets for 95 yards—all season-high marks for the 25-year-old. His 16.5 fantasy points resulted in a top-10 finish, his first since the 2025 finale but also his third in the last seven games.

While Strange likely won't find things as easy against a tougher Philadelphia Eagles opponent in Week 5, he'll look to carry his momentum into the contest and have another strong outing.

articles.title: Who is Michael Penix Jr.’s wife Olivia? Meet the woman behind the Falcons star as they expect their first baby
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. and his wife Olivia are preparing for a new chapter away from the football field.
articles.body: Michael Penix Jr. and his wife Olivia are preparing for a new chapter away from the football field. The Atlanta Falcons quarterback and Olivia announced they are expecting their first child, with the baby due in spring 2027. The couple shared the news in a video on social media that showed Olivia’s baby bump, ultrasound images and a blanket announcing “Baby Penix, Spring 2027.” The announcement came only five months after their May wedding in Georgia, adding another major milestone to a relationship that began during Penix’s college years.Who is Olivia, Michael Penix Jr.’s wife?Olivia Carter, now Olivia Penix, grew up in Washington and has a background of her own in college athletics. She played soccer at the University of Nevada, Reno, before graduating in 2022. Her connection with Penix began during his time at the University of Washington, where he played quarterback before entering the NFL. The pair eventually made their relationship public, with their social media posts giving fans glimpses into their life together.Olivia has also been a familiar presence during an important period in Penix’s football career. Their relationship continued as he moved from college football to the NFL, and she supported him through the demanding period that followed his knee injury.Penix has previously spoken about the role Olivia played during his rehabilitation. In May, he said she helped keep him positive around the house as he recovered from the injury. That support has made her more than a familiar name around the Falcons quarterback’s personal life.When did Michael Penix Jr. and Olivia get married?Penix and Olivia married on May 2, 2026, at Chateau Elan in Braselton, Georgia. The wedding came after the couple got engaged in December 2024, shortly after Penix had established himself as an NFL starter.Their wedding was a notable moment during a difficult stretch for Penix. He was recovering from a torn ACL that had ended his previous season and was working toward a return. Olivia’s presence during that period gave the quarterback something important outside football as he worked through rehabilitation.The ceremony also drew several of Penix’s Falcons teammates, including Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts. Olivia later shared moments from the celebration, including photos marking their first weeks as husband and wife.When is Michael Penix Jr. and Olivia’s baby due?The couple’s first child is expected in spring 2027. Their announcement video, titled “A Short Love Story By The Penix’s,” showed the pair celebrating together before revealing ultrasound images and the baby announcement. Olivia also showed her growing bump in the video.The caption was simple: “Upgraded to mom and dad.”The timing makes the news especially notable. Penix has spent much of the past year dealing with football uncertainty, from ACL rehabilitation to his return as Atlanta’s quarterback. Now, as he continues building his career, he and Olivia are preparing for a very different responsibility.For Olivia, the pregnancy adds another chapter to a relationship that has grown alongside Penix’s rise from college quarterback to NFL starter. Their wedding came only months ago. articles.title: "Let’s go get a nice girl that works at Walmart": Madison Beer dragged into Justin Herbert’s struggles as 2-time Super Bowl champion makes surprising claim
articles.summary: LeSean McCoy has found a new reason for Justin Herbert's rough start, and it has nothing to do with the offensive line or the playbook.
articles.body: LeSean McCoy has found a new reason for Justin Herbert's rough start, and it has nothing to do with the offensive line or the playbook. On the Game Over podcast, the two-time Super Bowl champion suggested Herbert's relationship with pop star Madison Beer is affecting his play. The Chargers are 0-4, and Herbert has thrown six interceptions against four touchdowns. McCoy's claim is blunt and impossible to prove. It still landed, because Chargers fans are searching for any explanation. Los Angeles faces the Broncos in Week 5, and Herbert needs answers on the field.Why did LeSean McCoy blame Madison Beer for Justin Herbert's struggles?McCoy said something is clearly off with Herbert this season. He compared the quarterback's situation to Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift, arguing that dating a global star brings a spotlight not every player can handle. "Something's wrong with him this year," McCoy said. "I don't know if he didn't get married, but I know he's all in love with this girl that's famous, right? Everybody can't do that."The advice got sharper from there. "It ain't working for you. Go get [yourself] a regular girl. Let's go get a nice girl that works at Walmart. Because she is too much for him right now," he said.McCoy also pointed to the interceptions, which he sees as a decision-making problem. "I watched this dude in a cover three, a hook curl defender. He threw the [expletive] right to him. I'm like, what are you doing?" McCoy said. He described a similar throw the week before, this time into a middle safety.Asked if Herbert is a fraud, McCoy said no. "He's not a fraud. He's got to date better," McCoy said.Herbert and Beer's relationship has played out in public. Dating rumors began in August 2025, after they appeared together on the set of her music video. They later went public, showing up at Lakers and Dodgers games. In May 2026, Herbert played the romantic lead in her "Lovergirl" video, and in July he proposed on their first anniversary. They announced it on Instagram with the caption "Meet my fiancé."How bad have Justin Herbert's numbers been for the 0-4 Chargers?The numbers back up the concern. Herbert has completed 71 of 119 passes for 816 yards, four touchdowns and six interceptions. He has also been sacked 12 times. His 64.8 PFN QB Impact Score ranks 33rd among 34 qualifying quarterbacks.Twelve sacks in four games is three a week. Pressure like that rushes decisions, which may explain some of the throws McCoy criticized.The Chargers came into the year with big hopes after hiring Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator, and Herbert has not yet found a rhythm in the new system. That context makes McCoy's frustration easier to understand, even if his target is questionable.Nothing suggests Beer has played any part in the slump. The measurable problems are interceptions, sacks and a winless record. Those can be fixed on the practice field, not on a date night.A clean game against Denver would change the conversation fast, whatever McCoy says. articles.title: “Pat, learn from him”: Patrick Mahomes accused of doing too many commercials as fan tells Chiefs star to follow Tom Brady’s football first example
articles.summary: A Kansas City Chiefs fan took a hard-hitting aim at Patrick Mahomes’ massive on- and off-gridiron profile.
articles.body: A Kansas City Chiefs fan took a hard-hitting aim at Patrick Mahomes’ massive on- and off-gridiron profile. The fan argued that the quarterback should spend less time appearing in commercials and more time preparing for the football season.The fan also compared the three-time Super Bowl champion with Tom Brady. The fan stated that Brady’s legendary career was built on his relentless commitment to the game. He was never busy with commercials. He always sported a football-first mindset.Tom Brady vs. Patrick Mahomes is not new. But this fan offers a unique take. Because there’s a spice called commercial commitment. Let’s understand this fan’s perspective.Tom Brady unlike Patrick Mahomes entered commercials after retirementThe fan wrote an eye-opening comment on Patrick Mahomes’ intriguing Coors Light beer commercial.The comment read, “Maybe if Pat spent less time doing commercials and more time on his job, his 3-peat would have worked, and the 2025 opener wouldn’t have been an embarrassment yesterday.Say what you will about [Tom] Brady, but I never recall seeing him in every single commercial during his career, and Tom was never posting pics of his 2-day Euro trip in the middle of the week that he did every other week during the season.Come to think of it, he never lived it up until he retired, and only now is Brady in commercials after he retired. Pat, learn from him. He wasn’t gifted with God-given abilities like you, but he’s outworked you and will clearly go on as the GOAT, and I’m a born-and-raised Chiefs fan. Remember, kid heroes get remembered, but legends never die…”This fan wrote their heart out; it doesn’t necessarily mean Mahomes spends more time on commercial commitments and less on football preparation. In fact, the two-time Super Bowl MVP doesn’t let commercials affect his football season.In a 2026 interview with GQ, Mahomes explained that his relentless focus on reaching the championship game shapes his entire offseason corporate calendar. He tells his marketing team not to schedule any commercial shoots before the end of February. This allows him to focus fully on football until after the Super Bowl.Patrick Mahomes’ commercial career and NFL preparationPatrick Mahomes has become one of the biggest advertising football stars in recent years.He has appeared in yearly campaigns for major brands like State Farm, Adidas, Head & Shoulders, Subway, and T-Mobile. Now, he appears in advertisements for his own coffee company, Throne Sport Coffee. He contributes to a serious off-gridiron business and boasts an enviable endorsement profile.Nevertheless, his extensive commercial presence does not equate to less time for football preparation. He has continued to produce at an elite level while maintaining his commercial presence. So the fan’s criticism is primarily perception.Just a day ago, he collaborated with Beats by Dre and shared five snapshots on Instagram. Now this comes after causing absolute havoc on the gridiron. Havoc meaning: going 4-0. Going undefeated! He continues to silence all the critics who declared he couldn’t come back wholly from a torn ACL!This is Stefon Diggs-style response to critics! Remember how Diggs came back from a torn ACL in 2025 playing for the New England Patriots? He still managed to record a 1,000-plus-yard season! Like he always had before the ACL injury. That’s how true players respond. That’s how true players show their love for their favorite game - football!Tom Brady’s commercial commitment whilst NFL careerAs for Tom Brady? The seven-time Super Bowl champion became particularly visible in commercials after his retirement. However, the FOX Sports analyst was not quiet during his playing years.The NFL legend had major endorsements with Movado, Vitamin Water, and Beautyrest Black, while he was still an active quarterback. Brady appeared in notable commercial shoots for Under Armor, Beautyrest, Dodge Dart, and UCG for Men during his NFL career.ABC News once reported that he traveled to New York after practice to shoot an advertisement, then returned to New England for the following morning’s practice. So, it’s not fair to say that Brady avoided commercials during his football years.The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers legend did have a strong reputation for discipline, preparation, nutrition, and training. But he also had a substantial commercial portfolio. His TB12 philosophy was closely associated with longevity and preparation. articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen’s divorce is back in the spotlight after a columnist offered a blunt take on what led to the end of their 13-year marriage. The retired NFL star and seven-time Super Bowl champion has faced years of scrutiny over the split, particularly after he returned to football in 2022. Now, comments from columnist Liz Jones, prompted by Lars Anderson’s new biography of Brady, have shifted attention toward the pressures surrounding the former couple and the choices Brady made during the final stage of his playing career.Tom Brady divorce debate takes a new turnJones has challenged the idea that Brady should carry the blame for the marriage ending. Writing about Anderson’s biography, Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, she argued that the book presents a more balanced account of the events surrounding the couple’s separation."I hate men but don't blame Tom Brady for his divorce... I pity him," Jones wrote.Her comments go beyond Brady and Bündchen’s relationship. Jones questioned the expectations placed on couples when one partner has an extremely demanding career. Brady’s decision to return for the 2022 NFL season had already put intense pressure on his personal life, with the quarterback spending another year focused on football before retiring for good in 2023.Jones also took aim at wider social expectations surrounding marriage, arguing that people can become dissatisfied even when they appear to have achieved a great deal."Women are always complaining their husband doesn't work hard enough, but when he does, we whine," Jones wrote. "Most women rejoice when their husband is always working. So, despite being a misandrist, I don't entirely blame Tom for the split and feel this new book is, for the most part, a more balanced view of one of the most famous unconscious uncouplings of the modern era."Tom Brady reportedly changed his NFL plans after divorceThe discussion becomes even more significant when viewed against Brady’s final NFL season. After winning his seventh Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Brady briefly retired before returning in 2022. Tampa Bay reached the playoffs, but its season ended with a wild-card loss to the Dallas Cowboys.Anderson has since suggested that Brady may have continued playing had his family situation been different. He told GQ that Brady ultimately stepped away because the divorce had changed his priorities."I think if Tom could do it over again, he wouldn't have come back for that final season, but does that mean the marriage could have been saved? I have no idea," Anderson said. "But there also was a real sense in the Buccaneers' locker room that they had a team that could win it all. Clyde Christensen, who was a quarterback coach in Tampa and a wonderful man, said, 'We were hoping that Tom would actually come out of retirement again, because we think we could have gotten number eight that year.'"But Tom told him, 'Look, because of the divorce, it's changing so much and I don't know how I'm going to navigate this new portion of my life.' articles.title: Cameron Jordan Rips' Saints Blowout Loss to Falcons in Video, 'S--t Was Embarassing'
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan didn't mince words about the team's performance in Monday's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan didn't mince words about the team's performance in Monday's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.

Jordan told reporters after the game that "s--t was embarrassing" to describe how the Saints played.

Jordan further explained that Saints players needed to show more urgency because "there is a division rivalry here" and his hope is they will "be there early in the morning" to get back to work on what they need to fix.

The fun early-season effort by the Saints, starting with their near-comeback in Week 1 against the Detroit Lions and capped off by an upset win over the Baltimore Ravens the next week, has given way to real flaws on both sides of the ball.

Jordan and the defense, especially, got picked on against the Falcons. Atlanta ran for 205 yards and five touchdowns, including 145 yards from Bijan Robinson and three scores by Brian Robinson Jr.

The Saints have allowed at least 340 yards and 30 points in three of their first four games. Their offense isn't helping matters with eight giveaways, including an NFL-high five fumbles lost.

Tyler Shough leads the league with five fumbles and is tied for the lead with three fumbles lost.

As a result of the poor defense and turnover woes, the Saints are constantly trying to dig themselves out of holes. They have trailed in every game this season and have fallen behind by at least 11 points three times.

Week 5 could be a good litmus test for how bad things can get for the Saints defense when they host the Minnesota Vikings.

Minnesota has scored fewer points in the last three games combined (38) than it did in Week 1 (39).

One thing working in the Saints' favor is the NFC South once again looks rather pedestrian. The Falcons and Carolina Panthers are tied for the division lead with matching 2-2 records.

A win over the Vikings on Sunday would have the Saints right back in the NFC South mix.

The Atlanta Falcons' X account reveled in the team's dominant, 45-24 road win over the New Orleans Saints on Monday night.

When the game started, Saints fans were juiced up for a meaningful and emotional game, as it took place on the 20th anniversary of their first game back at the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.

In that particular game, the Saints beat the Falcons 23-3, spurred on by a Steve Gleason blocked punt returned for a touchdown.

The Falcons quickly seized momentum on Monday night and never gave it back, though, as Robinson rushed for a 59-yard touchdown less than two minutes into the game.

Atlanta never gave up the lead, and it led by as many as 28 points in the fourth quarter.

With Monday's win, the Falcons improved to 2-2 on the season and kept pace with the Carolina Panthers for the NFC South lead, while the Saints fell to 1-3.

Jason became an NFL star during his long Eagles career, while Kylie developed her own identity through her work, family life and public appearances.Their story also has an unusual beginning. The pair met on Tinder in 2015, before Jason became an even bigger household name through his NFL career and the New Heights podcast with his brother, Travis Kelce.The age difference has never appeared to be the defining feature of their relationship. Her background in field hockey and involvement in community initiatives have helped make her more than simply an NFL wife. articles.title: 1 Trade That Could Turn Season Around for NFL's 0-4 Teams
articles.summary: Five teams remain winless after the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL season. While only the 1992 San Diego Chargers have managed to rebound from an 0-4 start to reach the playoffs, the league's current 17-game schedule does give these moribund squads more hope for a turnaround.
articles.body:
Five teams remain winless after the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL season. While only the 1992 San Diego Chargers have managed to rebound from an 0-4 start to reach the playoffs, the league's current 17-game schedule does give these moribund squads more hope for a turnaround.

There may be enough games remaining on the schedule to go on the type of run needed to clinch a postseason berth, but any club sitting at 0-4 after a full month faces significant obstacles to such a turnaround.

These slumping franchises shouldn't hesitate to leverage the trade market to shake things up. There's no better way to acquire an impact player who could jump-start a flatlining offense or defense, even if such a maneuver will come at the cost of some valuable draft capital.

Whether that's worth it remains to be seen, but any front office with serious aspirations of bouncing back from an 0-4 start may need to consider an aggressive move.

With that in mind, let's highlight one potential season-saving trade each of the NFL's winless teams should consider.

Houston Texans: Bolster Struggling Defense with Daron Payne

Washington Commanders receive: 2027 fourth- and fifth-round draft picks

The Houston Texans have won a playoff game in each of the last three seasons, but that streak looks to be in serious jeopardy after an 0-4 start.

The defense has been a surprising weak point for this franchise and cratered in a must-win Week 4 matchup against the in-state rival Dallas Cowboys.

After CeeDee Lamb went nuclear with 17 catches for 189 yards and a game-winning touchdown against his side, edge-rusher Will Anderson Jr. pointed out that a chunk of blame for the team's Week 4 shortcomings falls on the defensive line (per Yahoo Sports' Matt Young ):

"We've got to do a better job of everybody having each other's back. We play (man-to-man coverage) and we can't have him out there like that. We've got to have his back. Look at the D-line, we've got to keep rushing, keep trying to get home through all the (chip blocks) and everything like that."

While the Texans have game-changers such as Anderson and Danielle Hunter in the defensive trenches, the interior hasn't looked nearly as strong as it did last year. Getting another big body who can help shut down the run and disrupt in the backfield might help Houston save its season.

Daron Payne could be the needle-mover the Texans need right now. He's squandering his prime on a listless Washington Commanders team that is 1-3 and trending towards another lost season. While he'll face a tall task getting Houston back into contention, the AFC South race is winnable and the Texans have most of the other pieces in place required to make history.

A front that includes Anderson, Hunter and Payne could give Houston a more formidable front and improve its chances of a turnaround.

Factor in DeMeco Ryans' elite defensive scheming, and it's hard to see the Texans not going on a run if they swing for the fences and find a way to add Payne to the mix.

Los Angeles Chargers: Take a Chance on Marvin Harrison Jr.

Los Angeles Chargers receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

Arizona Cardinals receive: 2027 third-round draft pick

The Los Angeles Chargers' 0-4 start is perhaps the biggest surprise of the 2026 NFL season's first month. The team was expected to be a legitimate Super Bowl contender, getting a massive boost from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's decision to join forces with head coach Jim Harbaugh.

The offense has looked anything but competitive with McDaniel calling the shots. The team ranks a pitiful No. 29 in scoring, averaging just 16.8 points per game. The passing offense is of particular concern, generating just 185.3 yards per game and accounting for a meager four touchdowns against six interceptions.

While injuries to the likes of left tackle Rashawn Slater and top wideout Ladd McConkey haven't helped L.A.'s cause, it's become clear there isn't enough talent here to compete. A trade for an immensely talented but underperforming wideout in Marvin Harrison Jr. could benefit all parties.

The Arizona Cardinals stunned the Bolts in the opener despite MHJ contributing just one catch for 33 yards in the 26-14 victory. He's remained a relative non-factor for the club over the last three games and has a modest 5/85/1 line on 12 targets going into Week 5.

It's the latest in what has been a steady regression for a receiver who once seemed destined for greatness. After tallying 885 yards and eight touchdowns on 62 catches as a rookie, Harrison only caught 41 balls for 608 yards and four touchdowns last season and is now on pace to finish 2026 with 361 yards and four scores on 21 receptions.

A change of scenery could be exactly what Harrison needs to rejuvenate his career. It could also be the missing piece for a broken Chargers passing offense that is falling apart around quarterback Justin Herbert.

While Los Angeles would be doomed if Harrison continues to struggle following a trade, the team is already well on its way to missing the playoffs and has little left to lose at this juncture.

Miami Dolphins: Roll the Dice on Brian Thomas Jr.

Miami Dolphins receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr.

Jacksonville Jaguars receive: 2027 third-round draft pick

The Miami Dolphins entered the 2026 NFL season with low expectations and an 0-4 start is hardly shocking. It's now up to the front office to decide if the club should try to turn things around now or wait until the offseason to make major moves.

The team has issues up-and-down the roster, ranking bottom-three in total and passing offense in addition to coming in dead-last in scoring offense. The defense is faring a bit better and ranks towards the middle of the pack in most major categories, but isn't anywhere near good enough to carry the team to respectability.

While it's far more likely the 'Phins will become a seller leading up to the November 10 trade deadline, they could take a stab at trying to win some games this year while also preparing for the future by trading for Jacksonville Jaguars wideout Brian Thomas Jr.

Thomas' value has plummeted as his sophomore slump has continued into his third NFL season. Although the 2024 first-round pick quickly jumped out as one of the league's top wideouts when he tallied 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns on 87 receptions as a rookie, it's gone completely downhill since.

With BTJ only posting a 48/707/2 stat line last year and contributing just 105 yards and one score on nine catches over the first four weeks of 2026, a split with the Jags is starting to feel inevitable.

Miami could capitalize on Thomas' potential availability and take a cost-effective shot at unearthing its next WR1. If the 23-year-old were to return to the elite form he displayed as a rookie, the Dolphins could lock him down to a long-term extension and develop him alongside whichever passer they wind up drafting to create the nucleus of the passing game for years to come.

At worst, the 'Phins lose out on a mid-round pick that may not have panned out anyway. It's the type of low-risk, high-reward move this franchise needs to make if it wants to quickly rebuild and get back into contention.

Buyers or Sellers for NFL's Most Surprising Teams 🏈

Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Ask Mac Jones to Save Another Season

Tampa Bay Buccaneers receive: QB Mac Jones

San Francisco 49ers receive: Conditional 2027 third-round draft pick

When the Tampa Bay Buccaneers issued a blockbuster contract extension to Baker Mayfield right before the 2026 NFL season kicked off, they probably didn't expect an undrafted rookie to be their starting quarterback with the season on the line in Week 4.

Mayfield is regarded as one of the league's toughest players and hadn't missed a single game during his first three seasons in Tampa. That changed when he dislocated his right thumb in Week 3, an injury that is expected to keep him out for several more weeks.

With Jalon Daniels at the reins, the Bucs unsurprisingly collapsed in a must-win showdown against the Green Bay Packers. The UDFA passer wasn't utterly terrible, but he still looked raw in a 19-of-27 passing, one-touchdown, two-interception performance.

Given how dire the situation has become leading up to Week 5, Tampa's brass should call up the San Francisco 49ers and see what it will take to pry Mac Jones away.

Jones was able to save the Niners' 2025 season when Brock Purdy went down for an extended stretch in the opener, leading the team to five wins in his eight starts. If he could step in and help the Bucs string together a handful of victories while Mayfield is sidelined, the team would still have a shot in what looks to be another wide-open NFC South race.

Jones would be costly and doesn't profile as a long-term option in Tampa due to his expiring contract and expected suitors this offseason, but shipping over a conditional pick (one that scales based on how the Bucs finish the season) for a vastly improved chance at making the playoffs could be worth the price of admission.

Tennessee Titans: Swap Tony Pollard for Jerry Jeudy

Tennessee Titans receive: WR Jerry Jeudy

Cleveland Browns receive: RB Tony Pollard

The Tennessee Titans are off to an 0-4 start for the second consecutive season. While they've shown glimpses of improvement, this franchise still has a long way to go.

Although Tennessee is probably gearing up for a fire sale that will see veterans like Tony Pollard, Calvin Ridley and Jeffery Simmons sent off in exchange for draft capital around the trade deadline, the club could try to find a comfortable middle ground by dealing for a youthful talent who can help in 2026 and beyond.

While there are needs across the board, Tennessee has to bolster the passing game to feel confident about quarterback Cam Ward's future. While No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate is starting to break out and Wan'Dale Robinson has been a decent safety valve for the signal-caller, no other Titans wideout has more than five catches on the year.

Jerry Jeudy could provide a shot in the arm as a dangerous No. 3 option. While he's in his seventh NFL season, the 2020 first-round pick is still only 27 years old with multiple years remaining on his current contract. He had an impressive 90/1,229/4 campaign in 2024—his first with the Cleveland Browns—but has fallen out of favor with the new regime, catching just five balls for 62 yards so far in 2026.

Cleveland has ripped off three consecutive wins to move to 3-1 and is starting to think about the playoffs, but still needs to shore up the ground game to withstand the long season.

No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed 31 rushing yards on the year, making Pollard an intriguing trade option for the club.

Although one-for-one swaps are rare in the NFL, a Jeudy-for-Pollard trade makes sense for both sides and could help each accomplish their goals in 2026.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes gets a rare “better than everyone” verdict from Kay Adams as Joe Burrow and Josh Allen face fresh scrutiny
articles.summary: Kay Adams has picked her quarterback, and it is Patrick Mahomes.
articles.body: Kay Adams has picked her quarterback, and it is Patrick Mahomes. The "Up & Adams" host made the call after Kansas City beat the undefeated Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 on Sunday to move to 4-0. Mahomes finished with 225 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-30 passing, a modest line that Adams still found convincing, even with the ground game doing most of the work. Her case rests on one idea: Mahomes is never the reason the Chiefs lose. She backed it by pointing to late mistakes from Joe Burrow and Josh Allen, whose teams both lost in Week 4.Why does Kay Adams think Patrick Mahomes is better than every other quarterback?Adams did not hedge. In a clip shared by her show, she put it plainly.“Patrick Mahomes is the best quarterback, and he’s better than the best quarterback that you think is the best because he is never the reason the Chiefs lose,” Adams said.That is a different kind of argument from the usual stats debate. She is ranking who gives his team the fewest ways to lose. Kenneth Walker III ran for 177 yards and two scores, so Mahomes did not need a huge passing day. Adams had no problem with that.“Patrick is so disciplined. He will never lose the game. And even when it’s a game like yesterday that’s more about the run game. I don’t want to hear it,” she said.She also credited his feel for when to push and when to pull back.“And his ability also to sort of discern and know exactly when to pull back and when to push. That is so hard to do.”He did push when it counted. In the fourth quarter, Mahomes hit Tyquan Thornton for 55 yards, which set up Walker's go-ahead touchdown. Kansas City scored again after a Raiders kickoff fumble, built an 11-point lead and held on for the win.How do Joe Burrow and Josh Allen's recent mistakes fit into her argument?“Burrow did not look great… at the end of last game. He’s going to figure it out. But I think it was costly in the win column. Josh Allen, interception, late game, costly,” Adams said.The details back her up on that narrow point. Buffalo lost 29-26 to the New England Patriots after Craig Woodson picked off Allen with 1:14 left, ending the Bills' final possession. Cincinnati fell 22-17 to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Burrow threw two interceptions, one in the red zone early in the fourth quarter. The Bengals' last drive ended when Chase Brown caught a pass for nine yards on fourth-and-10, one yard short.The wider numbers tell a more mixed story. Through Week 4, the PFN QB Impact Score has Mahomes fifth at 82.1, Allen seventh at 81.5 and Burrow twelfth at 79.1. Mahomes leads that pair, but he does not top the whole list. That gap is what makes Adams' view worth a second look. She is judging reliability, not volume. articles.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson reportedly dealing with sprained ankle, has 'outside' chance to play Week 5
articles.summary: Jackson did not play in the second half of Sunday's win over the Titans.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson reportedly suffered a sprained ankle during Sunday's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Jackson did not return to the field for the second half and was spotted leaving the locker room in a walking boot. An MRI was scheduled for Monday.

Per Rapoport, there remains an "outside" chance Jackson could play Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. Depending on how his recovery goes, he is also at risk of missing time. The ankle injury is not considered a long-term ailment or one that would require surgery.

If Jackson cannot go in Week 5, Tyler Huntley, who relieved Jackson against the Titans, would get the start. Huntley went 8-of-9 passing for 63 yards and added 16 rushing yards.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday, "I don't know the chances yet" of Jackson playing in Week 5, and did add, "I don't think it's going to be crazy long-term."

Jackson appeared to sustain the injury on a sack late in the first half by Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson. The Ravens quarterback was able to stand up from the tackle and walk off the field.

Replays showed that Jackson's left ankle got caughtand twisted under Johnson's body as Johnson sacked him from behind.

Before the injury, Jackson went 15 for 20 for 222 yards and two touchdowns, while adding 20 rushing yards.

Jackson has completed 70.8% of his passes, which, if he sustains that mark, would be a career high. The quarterback has thrown for 967 yards, 6 touchdowns and 1 interception so far. Jackson isn't running as much, but still has an additional 144 yards and another score on the ground.

The Ravens are tied with the Cleveland Browns atop the AFC North through four games. Both teams are 3-1, while the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals are 2-2.

articles.title: In 2014, a Tennessee couple paid 58 cents for a West Point sweater at a North Carolina Goodwill; months later, experts authenticated it as Vince Lombardi's, and it sold for $43,020
articles.summary: A sweater picked up for just 58 cents at a North Carolina Goodwill turned out to have a remarkable connection to football history.
articles.body: A sweater picked up for just 58 cents at a North Carolina Goodwill turned out to have a remarkable connection to football history. Tennessee couple Sean and Rikki McEvoy bought the black-and-gold sweater in 2014, initially intending to take it to their vintage clothing store in Knoxville. Months later, they realised it could have belonged to legendary coach Vince Lombardi. According to Heritage Auctions, the sweater was later sold at its Sports Platinum Night auction for $43,020 in February 2015, turning a tiny thrift-store purchase into a five-figure sports collectible.A 58-cent Goodwill discoveryThe McEvoys found the sweater at a Goodwill outlet in Asheville, North Carolina, where clothing and other goods were sold by weight. The price worked out to just 58 cents for the sweater. At first, there was no indication that the ordinary-looking piece of clothing had any major historical value. The couple planned to take it back to Knoxville for their vintage clothing business.The discovery came a few months later when the couple were watching a television documentary about Lombardi. They noticed an image of the famous coach wearing a sweater that looked almost identical to the one they had bought at Goodwill. That prompted them to take a closer look at their find. A tag inside the sweater helped confirm their suspicion.The clue that linked it to LombardiInside the sweater was a white cotton swatch with the words “Lombardi 46” handwritten on it. Heritage Auctions said the marking clearly identified the garment as belonging to Lombardi. The coach wore the sweater during his years at West Point, where he served as an assistant to the head coach of the U.S. Army Black Knights. His time at the military academy came before he entered the NFL.Lombardi's West Point years were an important part of his coaching career. He later made his NFL debut with the New York Giants in 1954 before becoming one of the most celebrated coaches in American football. Photographs from the period also showed Lombardi wearing the same distinctive black-and-gold sweater, giving the thrift-store discovery an additional connection to its original owner.How the sweater reached GoodwillThe sweater had an interesting history of its own before it ended up on a Goodwill outlet rack. Heritage Auctions reported that it had been donated by the widow of Bill Wannamaker, who coached at West Point alongside Lombardi during the 1940s and early 1950s. That connection helped explain how a garment associated with Lombardi eventually found its way into a charity outlet. The piece was ultimately consigned for auction, where its history attracted collectors.The auction house also chose to donate its entire seller's commission from the sale to Goodwill. Heritage said the decision was made in recognition of Wannamaker's contribution to football history and the family's original wish that the sweater help raise money for the charity.From thrift-store clothing to sports historyOnce the sweater's connection to Lombardi became clear, it was no longer simply a vintage piece of clothing. It became a tangible reminder of the period when Lombardi was developing his coaching career at West Point. The handwritten identification, period photographs and its connection to a former West Point coach all added to its significance.The difference between its original price and its eventual auction result was striking. The McEvoys had paid only 58 cents for the sweater, while an anonymous collector bidding by telephone ultimately paid $43,020 for it.A tiny purchase with a huge payoffThe Lombardi sweater is an example of how valuable sports history can sometimes turn up in places where shoppers least expect it. articles.summary: Founded by Travis Kelce in 2015, 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education,
articles.body: Founded by Travis Kelce in 2015, 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, STEM, and the arts. Its “Ignition Lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization Operation Breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.Through the Ignition Lab program, under-resourced teenagers from Kansas City neighborhoods can explore STEM and entrepreneurship with mentorship, equipment, and hands-on learning.Although 87 & Running Foundation’s Instagram account has seen no recent activity, its charitable work continues through initiatives like Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab.According to the foundation’s website, the Ignition Lab program serves about 700 students daily. Young people have opportunities to learn, create, develop practical skills, and explore several pathways that could shape their future education and careers.Travis Kelce’s foundation continues youth work amid financial scrutiny87 & Running Foundation’s official Instagram account has not posted any content since January 2026. At the same time, social media fans raised money-laundering allegations against the foundation.According to The Arizona Republic, the foundation’s IRS filings reported raising about $1.5 million and spending roughly $1.1 million over a multi-year period [2021 to 2024]. Only 41 cents of every dollar was reportedly directed to charitable programs.CharityWatch executive director, Laurie Styron, told The Arizona Republic that, “players and their managers need to stop using charities this way. Don’t get creative. Don’t look for loopholes.If you establish a charity, stop mixing in business interests or using friends to operate it. Do it the right way or don’t do it at all. There are a lot of ways for players to give back without founding their own charity.”Despite this growing tension, Travis Kelce’s foundation reportedly continued its work through the Ignition Lab program with Operation Breakthrough. Operation Breakthrough is a nonprofit organization that provides educational and developmental opportunities for children and families in Kansas City.Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation funds and powers its Ignition Lab program. The program gives 14- to 18-year-old teenagers access to resources that promote innovation, technical learning, and entrepreneurial thinking. This partnership expands 87 & Running Foundation’s financial support to create opportunities for young people.Donna Kelce joins students for special Chiefs experienceIn August 2026, Operation Breakthrough expressed heartfelt gratitude to Travis Kelce for arranging an opportunity for Ignition Lab students. The students attended the Kansas City Chiefs’ first preseason game from Kelce’s suite at Arrowhead Stadium.The organization wrote on Instagram, “Talk about a suit surprise! Thanks to Travis Kelce, our Ignition Lab students experienced the Chiefs’ first preseason game from his suite at Arrowhead!”The post also mentioned that the students met Travis Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, during the outing. This experience gave participating students a heartfelt opportunity to enjoy a Chiefs game. It also helped them create lasting memories connected to their Kansas City community.Ed Kelce connects family legacy with childrenThe 87 & Running Foundation’s 2025 annual report speaks for the foundation’s continued charitable work.Their website also provides information about its programs and partnerships. However, their collaboration with Operation Breakthrough through Ignition Lat provides additional insight into the foundation's activities and its connection to the Kelce family. In particular, Travis Kelce’s father, Ed Kelce.On September 17, 2026, Operation Breakthrough shared a post on Instagram about Ed Kelce visiting. The father of NFL legends Jason and Travis Kelce read to first-grade students and showed them the cutest, rarest childhood photos of Jason and Travis.The organization wrote, “Storytime with a side of Kelce family throwbacks! Ed Kelce stopped by to read to our first graders, then gave them a peek at Travis and Jason when they were little, just like them! Thank you, Ed, for sharing your time and a little family history with our children!”Yesterday, it was Travis Kelce’s 37th birthday on October 5, 2026. The little angels at Operation Breakthrough sent warmest wishes for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end through an adorable Instagram reel.The organization collaborated on the post with 87 & Running Foundation and called it, “Little voices, BIG birthday wishes! Happy birthday, Travis! articles.title: Arch Manning confronts growing NFL Draft expectations with one clear message about his future beyond Texas
articles.summary: Arch Manning has one more year of college eligibility, and he is not rushing to talk about what comes after Texas.
articles.body: Arch Manning has one more year of college eligibility, and he is not rushing to talk about what comes after Texas. The 22-year-old quarterback told PEOPLE he is taking things day by day as questions about the Heisman and his future keep piling up. Texas is 4-0 and ranked No. 1, yet Manning admitted he did not play his best in the win at Tennessee. His mother says that is just who he is. With the Red River Rivalry against Oklahoma days away, his attention is fixed on just one game.What has Arch Manning said about his future beyond Texas?Asked whether he has another year of eligibility, Manning kept it short. “I do,” Arch smiles in a Zoom with PEOPLE. “Yes, ma’am. I’m taking it day by day.”That reply does not point either way, and it may not be meant to. Manning is in his second season as the Longhorns starter and has faced Heisman questions for two years. Texas, now No. 1 in the country, has given him plenty to talk about, including a 24-23 comeback win at home over Ohio State on Sept. 12. He still sticks to the simple answer.He explained why. “I try to remind myself, like, I used to dream about playing football, you know, at the University of Texas, being the starting quarterback for college,” he says.Why does Ellen Manning call her son a perfectionist?Ellen watched the Tennessee game from a suite above Neyland Stadium with her husband, Cooper, Archie and Peyton. Texas won, but Arch left unhappy with his own play. She was not surprised. “Arch is extremely tough on himself,” Ellen, 57, told PEOPLE in an interview for the heart-health supplement Humann.Self-praise does not come easy to him, she added. “He will never come off and say, ‘God, that was great, I played great.’ ”She laughed as she said the rest. “You know, he’s a perfectionist. And hopefully that’ll serve him well. He’s killing it, and nobody’s gonna have a perfect game, ever.”Arch seems to agree. “I need to start making the most out of these games,” he said with a smile.How are Eli and Peyton Manning helping Arch Manning?Arch values it. “Anytime you have two elite quarterbacks as your uncles helping you out and giving you advice and support, it helps a lot,” Arch tells PEOPLE.Ellen said the calls are not constant. The uncles live in different cities and have families of their own. “What’s nice is they’re there, you know?” she said. “It’s literally, they’re there as a resource, and it’s wonderful.”Eli has kept his advice mostly on the field. Earlier this month, Arch drew criticism for comments on an AI video featuring Texas coach Steve Sarkisian and ESPN’s Holly Rowe. Eli addressed it with Front Office Sports. “Most of my advice is more football stuff,” he said. “He’ll have to figure out that media on his own, a lot of it is just growing pains.”Outside the family, his favorite NFL quarterback is a different name entirely. “I really like watching Josh Allen,” Arch says, smiling, as he holds up a bobblehead.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brock Purdy earns first career monthly honor after 49ers’ unbeaten start
articles.summary: thenews2.com/Depositphotos Brock Purdy earns first monthly honor Brock Purdy, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback, earned NFC Offensive Player of the Month f...
articles.body:
Brock Purdy, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback, earned NFC Offensive Player of the Month for September 2026, the first monthly honor of his NFL career after San Francisco opened the season with a 3-0 record.

Purdy completed 60 of 83 passes for 789 yards, 9 touchdowns, and 1 interception through three games. He also added 93 rushing yards, 8 rushing first downs, and 1 touchdown on 10 carries.

Purdy completed 72.3% of his passes during San Francisco's first three games, helping the 49ers average 32.7 points per game during an unbeaten September to open the 2026 season.

His 133.1 passer rating led NFL quarterbacks after Week 3, while his 9 touchdown passes were tied for the league lead. San Francisco then defeated Denver 24-14 in Week 4 to improve to 4-0.

Purdy opened the 2026 season in Melbourne against the Los Angeles Rams, throwing 3 touchdown passes as San Francisco began with a 27-7 victory at Melbourne Cricket Ground in the league's Australia opener.

That Week 1 performance produced a 105.6 passer rating and began a three-game September stretch with at least 2 touchdown passes and a rating above 100 in every contest San Francisco played.

Purdy followed the opener by completing 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and 2 touchdowns against Miami, helping San Francisco earn a 35-13 Week 2 victory in its home opener at Levi's Stadium.

He also rushed for 30 yards and 1 touchdown against the Dolphins. That performance earned him the NFC Offensive Player of the Week before his September Player of the Month honor arrived after Week 3.

Purdy threw for a season-high 297 yards and 4 touchdowns in San Francisco's 36-30 Week 3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27 in Santa Clara, California.

Two touchdown passes to George Kittle helped San Francisco finish the close game and remain 3-0. The 49ers then turned their attention to Denver before defeating the Broncos 24-14 in Week 4 to improve to 4-0.

Purdy added measurable rushing production during September, gaining 93 yards, producing 8 first downs, and scoring once on 10 carries through San Francisco's first three victories of the 2026 regular season.

His rushing touchdown came against Miami, when he gained 30 yards on 3 attempts and added another scoring option to an offense already producing efficiently through the air during the Week 2 victory.

Purdy took no sacks during San Francisco's first three games, giving the 49ers a clean passing platform while the offense started the season with strong protection and efficient quarterback play across all three victories.

That sack-free stretch accompanied 9 touchdown passes and only 1 interception, helping San Francisco reach October unbeaten while maintaining one of the NFL's most productive early passing attacks through the first three games.

Purdy became San Francisco's first quarterback since Steve Young in 1995 to open a season with three straight games featuring at least 2 touchdown passes and a passer rating above 100 in each appearance.

San Francisco also led the NFL with 7.35 yards per play after Week 3, giving Purdy's historical quarterback marker added context within one of the league's most efficient offenses during September.

San Francisco converted 90.0% of its red zone trips into touchdowns through three games, the NFL's best rate after Week 3 and another measure of the offense's September efficiency near the goal line.

The 49ers also ranked second in total scoring with 98 points, giving Purdy's individual production support from an offense that consistently finished drives during its unbeaten opening month of the 2026 regular season.

Fred Warner praised Purdy after the Arizona victory, calling him amazing and saying San Francisco's offense was humming. At the same time, the defense needed to handle its own responsibilities during the team's unbeaten start.

Warner's comments followed a 36-30 result in which Purdy threw 4 touchdown passes, helping San Francisco remain unbeaten and stay alone atop the NFC West after three games of the 2026 season.

Fun fact: Purdy once punctured his left hand on a saguaro cactus while playing paintball with high school teammates in the Arizona desert.

San Francisco entered Week 4 at 3-0 after victories over the Rams, Dolphins and Cardinals, leaving the 49ers alone in first place in the NFC West as the calendar moved into October.

After Week 4, San Francisco improved to 4-0 with a 24-14 victory over Denver. Seattle moved to 3-1, while the Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals fell to 2-2 and 1-3, respectively, leaving the 49ers alone atop the division entering Week 5.

Purdy and the 49ers hosted the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 4 and earned a 24-14 victory. Purdy completed 19 of 30 passes for 218 yards and 2 touchdowns as San Francisco improved to 4-0.

Denver entered the game at 2-1 but fell to 2-2 after the loss. San Francisco now heads to Seattle for its Week 5 NFC West matchup on October 11, with the Seahawks entering the week at 3-1.

Travis Kelce broke an all-time NFL record without realizing he was even close to it , adding another milestone to a career already defined by postseason production and longevity.

Purdy's September included efficient passing, rushing production, 9 touchdown throws, and no sacks across three victories, giving the NFL a broad statistical record behind the first monthly honor of his professional career.

San Francisco paired Purdy's performance with strong red zone scoring, 98 total points, and a 3-0 record, placing his individual award within a wider team start that featured consistent offensive production throughout September.
